I left my kitten on a Monday because he was jaundiced and had no appetite. After several tests, they discovered he had feline triaditis.
I visited him every day, and every day I received feedback (the only positive point), however, they always gave me false hope. Constant budget updates to the point where they didn't even know how much was left to pay, how much had already been paid...
On Friday, they caused him pulmonary edema due to the treatments they tried.
I was left with a strong impression of amateurism.
It's sad, we leave our most precious possession in the hands of other people who seem to be playing at being doctors.
What is certain is that after 5 days, which was the time they initially indicated would be the length of his stay in the ward, he died during our visit. He was suffering, we asked for euthanasia but they didn't even bother with that, as he died before they arrived with the equipment...
It's outrageous, we spent about 1500 euros to torture our little boy for 5 days before he died.
I don't recommend it, and it's not even about the money, which, although not infinite, we do everything for.
If I had known it was going to be like this, it would have been better to have euthanized her from the start and end the suffering.

I really wish I had found this vet much sooner! I highly recommend Dra. Madalena… I wish she could be my doctor too lol. She was muito simpática & great with my cat… who was very scared before his vaccinations but perfectly at ease & happy again when he came back out so they took great care of him<3

I was also very late but they were still able to see me so thanks again!

Ramona was in this team's care for the last year of her life, through four hospitalizations and multiple surgeries for a complex, aggressive condition. Through it all, they treated her, and me, with extraordinary kindness, always making space to see her and responding promptly to every call. Ramona was a fearful girl by nature, but she was never afraid there. She loved everyone on this team, and even though the clinic became a second home to her because of her illness, it was full of genuine warmth for her.
I want to especially thank Dr. Inês Oliveira, who tried everything to save my girl and never gave up on her, and Gabriela and Elisabete at the front desk, whose compassion carried me through some of my hardest hours. This team truly loves the animals in their care. They gave my girl the IV treatments and constant care her condition required in moments I couldn't be the one doing it myself, no matter how much I wished I could have. I will be forever grateful to them.

What happened to Oscar during his hospitalization is, to me, serious and unacceptable.
Oscar was admitted because he could no longer walk, had little sensation in his hind limbs, and urinary incontinence. We were told there was a possibility of a spinal problem and that a CT scan would be crucial to reach a diagnosis.
We trusted the team and followed all the instructions. During his hospitalization, we received contradictory information. An alteration in his blood glucose was detected, and later we were told that the machine was broken and that the values ​​would not be reliable. Meanwhile, Oscar started walking again and was discharged without us having the CT scan results and without a diagnosis that explained the episode.
At discharge, there were also costs higher than initially indicated, including procedures for which I do not recall being previously informed or giving consent.
The most serious thing happened later: we were informed that there was an error related to the CT scan, making it necessary to repeat the exam. Oscar underwent general anesthesia for an examination that did not produce the expected result due to a technical failure. And, after all this, it was suggested that he undergo the procedure again.
At this moment, Oscar continues to be medicated, but we still lack a clear explanation about the diagnosis, the cause of what happened, the purpose of all the medication, and how long he should take it.
In a veterinary hospital with 24-hour service, I do not consider acceptable a succession of failures in essential equipment, contradictory information, the absence of a clear diagnosis, and failures in communication about procedures and costs.
We are talking about the health of an animal, general anesthesia, and clinical decisions that require rigor, transparency, and responsibility.
I demand complete clarification on everything that happened, access to clinical records and examinations performed, justification of the procedures and amounts charged, and a formal response regarding the failures that occurred.

I cannot recommend OneVet.

We were assessed by Dr. Gonçalo Simões on May 11 and returned for a CT scan on May 13. From the start, communication and coordination were poor.

We were told our dog's surgery was scheduled, only to call the day before and be informed that no surgery had actually been booked. At a time when we were already worried about our dog's health, this was both frustrating and upsetting.

We then spent weeks trying to get answers and eventually had to return in person just to collect the scan results. Getting clear information about the diagnosis felt unnecessarily difficult, and we repeatedly had to follow up before receiving the report and understanding what was actually going on. As pet owners, we were left feeling confused and uncertain during a period when we were simply trying to make the right decisions for our dog.

To make matters worse, we were quoted almost three times more for surgery than another hospital and were advised that a €400 3D-printed model would be required as part of the surgical planning process, only to later learn that it was not necessary. We also had to repeat X-rays elsewhere.

In the end, we lost three weeks and valuable time that could have been spent moving forward with treatment. The experience cost us unnecessary time, money, and stress. When it comes to a pet's health, clear communication and proper coordination matter, and unfortunately that was not our experience.

I've been going to this vet for 6 years and I highly recommend them!

My 3-year-old dog, Oreo, developed several health problems, and they were always incredible throughout.

Last year I took her in urgently because she was having seizures. Every month after that, I went to the vet at least once or more, and they were incredibly helpful. When I left her there for the last time, after she was taken inside to be stabilized, I started having a panic attack, and the people at the entrance were incredibly helpful in trying to assist.

Every time I called, regardless of the time, including when I called in the middle of the night while my dog ​​was hospitalized, they were always incredibly helpful.

Even when my Oreo passed away, the entire hospital team was amazing to me, and I am immensely grateful for all the time they dedicated to helping Oreo suffer as little as possible and be happy.

I have to thank all the doctors, nurses, and any staff member who helped. I often think about the lady who had to give me the bad news over the phone because I genuinely felt that it was difficult for her too. Everyone cares about the well-being of my dogs and wants the best for them.

Thank you to the whole team!

Words fail me to express my gratitude for all the care you gave my Luna, right up until the end. I had the privilege of visiting Luna while she was hospitalized and saw how well she was treated. I thank all the professionals at this clinic, every single one, for every tear that came to comfort me, every word, and for all the love you gave Luna. And when the time comes for my Nina, she will be cared for in your hands. My deepest gratitude to you all.

Today I went to this hospital with my cat Walquiria and I received excellent care.

I took my dog ​​Mel to be spayed at this veterinary hospital and the experience was excellent from start to finish. From the moment I arrived, I was always treated with great kindness, attention, and professionalism.
I want to give a special thank you to Dr. Luciana Pardini, who was extraordinary. Always very attentive, calm, and humane, she explained everything very clearly and gave me enormous confidence. Mel is a very nervous dog, and Dr. Luciana showed incredible care and sensitivity towards her, always treating her with affection and respect.
The surgery went very well, and upon discharge, all the post-operative instructions were explained in detail, showing a genuine concern for Mel's well-being. I left the hospital feeling calm, confident, and very grateful for all the care shown, from arrival to departure.
I recommend this veterinary hospital without any hesitation. Thank you to the entire team, and especially to Dr. Luciana Pardini, for the excellent work and dedication.
My Tuty was received at the veterinary hospital through AZP. He was seen quickly and received excellent care. From reception to the end of the treatment, everyone was impeccable. Ana Menezes

Today I took my cat, Frida, to the vet because she suspected she had a urinary tract infection. There were two vets, and one of them was Dr. Inês, who couldn't perform an ultrasound, do any other examination, or even give her any medication to calm her down, even though I helped. And another thing, they weren't wearing gloves; I had to ask them several times to put them on. The cat was screaming so loudly you could hear it on the corner, something that had never happened before… They didn't seem to care about helping. I don't know how it's possible to be so inhumane to animals.

I even paid over 90 euros just for the consultation, and my cat left injured and bleeding. They didn't even know where the blood was coming from; I had to show them that she was bleeding and that it was on her paw. She arrived fine and left in bad shape! Terrible service!

Absolutely blown away by the incredible quality of care I received here. Deeply moved by the kindness and efficiency of the staff, from receptionists to vets this was a remarkably qualified team and the standard of treatment is the best I have ever seen at a veterinary hospital. 10 stars, thank you so much to the team for everything.
Six hours of calling and no one bothers to answer...they must be playing cards...a disgrace.

I want to express my deepest gratitude to the entire team at the Berna Veterinary Hospital (Lisbon) for the care, affection, and dedication they showed to the little dog I rescued, abandoned at Corroios station.

Unfortunately, our little Maya didn't survive… But I'm certain that, on the day she was hospitalized, she was deeply loved, pampered, and treated with all the dignity that such a pure being deserves. It was a true team effort… it started with me at the moment of the rescue, but it was only possible to give her this opportunity thanks to you, who welcomed her with open arms.

A special thank you to Dr. Luciana, who fought alongside her during the surgery and gave her best, even knowing the case was complicated. Her dedication and humanity did not go unnoticed.

From the bottom of my heart, thank you all. Maya, if she were here, would certainly thank you all with all the love in the world. ♥️🐾

Two weeks ago (on June 12th), my cat Ofélia started limping on one paw out of nowhere, and after a short search, I decided to go to Onevet. Additionally, the decision was made because I had a discount voucher since Ofélia is a blood donor at BSA. I tried calling 5 times and had to wait half an hour for an answer.

The receptionists were friendly up to a point, sometimes giving short and rude answers, when I wasn't ignored. To make matters worse, I can't accept having only one veterinarian available in an emergency room. I waited about 2 hours for a 5-minute consultation that served to weigh her, feel her paw a little, and advise on X-rays. I agreed because I was worried and wanted to understand the reason for the problem. However, I thought that during this process, her paw would be examined more thoroughly. Especially since I never ruled out the possibility of it being a superficial wound – a cut, a cactus skewer, etc.

They told me the process would be brief, about 15 minutes, and that I couldn't be present. I waited more than half an hour for them to show me three x-rays and conclude that it wasn't a bone issue, but probably muscular. They prescribed medication (an anti-inflammatory), said they would get a second opinion from the orthopedist, and asked for feedback on her condition in the coming days.

Ofélia's condition remained the same during this period, with slight improvements. After finishing the medication, the veterinarian prescribed the same anti-inflammatory and analgesics and asked for feedback again. However, she warned me that the orthopedist concluded everything was fine. When I finished the medication for the second time, without significant changes, I was told I should schedule an appointment with the orthopedist for a second opinion. In my opinion, this advice made no sense at all because he had already given his positive opinion, but I agreed again out of desperation. They scheduled the appointment a week later, forcing me to buy another round of medication.

Last Tuesday (June 24th), already desperate with the situation, I decided to touch my cat's paw, hoping to find something. To my astonishment, I looked and immediately saw a dark stain. I used a flashlight and saw DRIED BLOOD around her paw, almost two weeks old. The attached video was recorded at that precise moment. I rushed her to another hospital where they removed a tiny fragment of glass from her paw!!

This experience was the height of negligence and irresponsibility!! How could they not have looked at the area in question? I can't describe the feeling of unprofessionalism this whole experience left me with. It's extremely sad to think that someone would take advantage of the love we have for our animals.

I absolutely do not recommend this establishment; it was very disappointing.

Not recommended. We went to a hospital emergency room with a dog that was vomiting blood and wouldn't eat, and the recommendation was to give her gastro-friendly food. They didn't do blood tests, they didn't do an ultrasound... if she didn't improve, they recommended blood tests and an ultrasound... why didn't they do it today? Because they didn't have staff on duty... in a hospital and in an emergency room. Thank you Dr. Miguel Godinho for absolutely nothing. And you don't need to give a generic answer because I will attach your medical report, dated day and time, immediately.

I do not recommend this veterinary clinic.
I took my dog ​​for a check-up, but nothing was done besides taking a blood sample for analysis. To this day, I am still waiting for the results, despite them promising to call me.

I requested that they assess my dog's paws, but the veterinarian refused to do so. Furthermore, they told me that my dog ​​needed to lose weight, but they provided no guidance on how to do it. What do they expect? That he starves?

A disappointing service and a frustrating experience. I feel I was cheated.
